aldemar.headline: Washington declares economic D-Day and oil falls — the market says the barrels were already gone
aldemar.standfirst: Monday the Treasury launched "Operation Economic Outcast" — 60+ entities, vessels and individuals across shipping, gold, aviation, tech and digital assets, with secondary sanctions threatening removal from the dollar system — and crude dropped 2.4% to 85.01. That reaction is the whole story: the blockade already stopped Iran's barrels, so sanctions hit revenue, not supply. Iran's rial fell to a record 2.02m per dollar and Mohsen Rezaei answered that if the pressure holds, "not a single drop of oil" transits Hormuz. Underneath, negative gamma deepened to −$11.1B with spot below the 7,673 flip; BAC reclaimed your 62 line, GOOG printed a new high for the position, and Aldemar's INTC broke to 85.14 intraday.

positions.title: 2 signals on BAC, INTC — read before the open

items.html: BAC — BAC +1.04% to 62.33 — reclaims the 62 line, but on rotation rather than on the curve. Friday's brief named the test: a reclaim of 62 would mark Thursday's break as expiry noise. It happened, with a 62.76 high on a day the Dow rose 0.26% while the Nasdaq fell 0.76%. Be precise about why, though — the 10-year fell 3bp to 4.70%, so this was defensive rotation buying banks, not the steepener firing. That distinction matters: the thesis is intact on price but its engine idled. Gabriel −3.18% on entry at −0.51R, stop 60.39 now 3.1% below; Aldemar −2.85% at −0.41R, stop 59.65, 4.3% below. Both recovered roughly 0.15R on the day. Jackson Hole later this week is what decides whether the curve resumes doing the work.

INTC — INTC −3.1% to 87.26 with an 85.14 low — BofA cuts its target to $145 while the CEO buys $12m. Six straight red closes and the intraday low took Aldemar to roughly −0.84R before the close pulled it back to −0.75R: three quarters of the risk unit is now spent, entry 105.81 against the 81.10 stop, which sits 7.1% below. The detail worth holding onto is that Vivek Arya — the same analyst whose CPU-TAM upgrade was the entry signal — cut his target from $160 to $145 but reiterated Buy, attributing the cut purely to 4–5% EPS dilution from the raise. The thesis was not withdrawn; it was re-priced for share count. CEO Lip-Bu Tan buying $12m alongside the offering is the counterweight. Nothing here changes the plan: the stop is the exit, and Nvidia's results Wednesday are the sector event that decides whether 85 was a bottom or a waypoint.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.

themes.right: Operation Economic Outcast · rial at record low · Hormuz threat renewed
themes.title: "Sever every economic lifeline" — the war moves onto the dollar system

items.html: Bessent unveils "Operation Economic Outcast": 60+ entities, vessels and individuals across five sectors, with expanded secondary sanctions. Shipping, gold, aviation, technology and digital assets — and the enforcement threat is removal from the US dollar system: "No one is above the reach of U.S. sanctions." A major action against a financial institution was previewed for later this week. The objective as stated is to "sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone."

Crude falls 2.4% to 85.01 on the sanctions announcement — the tell of the week. Sanctions that remove barrels normally lift the price. These did the opposite because the barrels are already blockaded: the measures attack revenue and finance, not physical supply. The war premium is now fully in the price of a strait that is already shut, which means further escalation on the financial track moves oil less than the market's instinct suggests.

Rezaei: continued pressure means "not a single drop of oil" through Hormuz — international participation would be "an act of war". Tehran's answer to financial strangulation is to threaten the one lever it still controls, and to widen the definition of combatant to anyone enforcing the sanctions. That is the escalation path that would reprice crude — not the sanctions themselves.

Iran's rial hits a record low of 2.02 million per dollar. The pressure campaign is working on the currency within a day of launch. A collapsing rial raises the odds of both outcomes — a regime that needs a deal, and a regime with nothing left to lose.

themes.note: The transmission is oil → inflation → the regime call, and Monday partially cut the first link: with crude down 2.4% and the strait's closure already priced, the marginal sanction now hurts Tehran more than it hurts the CPI path. That is quietly good for the book's macro backdrop — CPI y/y at 3.3 against the 2.5 floor gets a little breathing room if crude stays at 85 rather than 93. The risk that replaces it is binary rather than gradual: Rezaei's threat, or a strike on an enforcing party, would move oil in a single session rather than a week. In negative gamma, that kind of headline lands on a tape with nothing damping it.

world.title: Seven straight down days for Nvidia, and the whole market waiting on Wednesday

items.html: Nvidia falls 2.9% for a seventh consecutive losing session ahead of Wednesday's earnings; memory names drop on a new Chinese chip IPO filing. The bellwether has been sold for a week and a half straight into its own print — that is positioning, not information, and it cuts both ways violently on Wednesday. Micron and SanDisk fell on a Shanghai IPO filing from another Chinese memory firm, a reminder that the supply side of the AI trade now has a competitive-pressure story too.

S&P −0.28% to 7,652.86, Nasdaq −0.76%, Dow +0.26%, Russell −0.76%; VIX +4.8% to 15.85. A split tape: consumer staples and communication services up, energy and technology down. The Dow's green close against the Nasdaq's red is the same defensive rotation that lifted BAC — and volatility rising on a small index move is the negative-gamma signature.

Negative gamma deepens: net −$11.1B from −$2.2B, spot 7,652.86 sitting 0.26% below the flip at 7,672.58. The first full session of the unpinned tape did exactly what the mechanic predicts: a modest index decline with volatility rising underneath it. Dealers are now five times shorter gamma than at Friday's reset, so Wednesday's Nvidia print and the Jackson Hole signal land on a tape that amplifies rather than absorbs.

Gold makes another record as safe-haven demand builds; the 10-year eases 3bp to 4.70%. Sanctions targeting gold as a sanctions-evasion channel while gold itself makes records is the week's neatest irony — and the bid is broadening from war hedge to dollar-system hedge, which is precisely what an operation built on dollar exclusion invites.

weekly.headline: Gold's best week of the year against the book's hardest — and the war became the weather
weekly.standfirst: The week opened with a dead deadline and closed with a dead framework: the memorandum expired Monday, missiles landed off the UAE Tuesday, China-linked supertankers turned around Thursday, and by Friday Washington was asking a refusing Beijing to help sanction Tehran. Equities absorbed it slowly — the S&P lost 1.43%, chips roughly 10% as the AI-financing audit claimed Intel's $20B raise — while gold ran 6.6% to three records and crude added 5.4%. The book paid its first real tuition: Gabriel's INTC stopped out at exactly −1R on Tuesday, both BAC positions broke their 62 line after Walmart repriced the consumer, and GOOG quietly held the whole time. The market leaves the week in negative gamma for the first time all month.

Retail sales −0.6%, sentiment 51, then the biggest retailer in the country blinked (−8.8% Thursday, −10% on the week). For a bank long the US consumer's balance sheet, the credit side of the thesis is now live risk, with the steepener side still intact against it.Eurasia Business News · Seeking Alpha · 14–20 Aug
METALSGold +6.6% — three records in five sessions, accelerating into strength. War premium, debt concerns, and a Treasury forced to buy its own long bonds: the debasement trade graduated from hedge to position. It was the single most profitable trade on the board this week, and nobody had to pick a stock to have it.Yahoo Finance · TradingKey · 17–21 Aug

The discipline ledger matters as much as the P&L this week: Gabriel's INTC exit filled at exactly the planned 95.52 — a clean −1.00R, taken on schedule, with no slippage on a −6.6% day. That is the system doing precisely what it was built to do. The open book ends the week: Gabriel +0.79R on GOOG against −0.67R on BAC; Aldemar −0.55R on BAC and −0.64R on INTC, both inside their planned risk with stops standing.
